hypothesis: Stock reservation in reserveInventoryStep is guarded by the Locking module, whose default provider is in-memory and holds locks in a per-process Map. With two Medusa servers on one database, each server's lock is independent, so two carts each needing the single SOLO unit can both pass the availability check and both reserve it. I expect no_oversell to fail (two live reservations totalling 2 against 1 stocked) in some runs, and possibly reserved_matches_reservations if the counter write also races.

The complete route calls completeCartWorkflow with no cart-level lock of its own; the only guard against double completion is the workflow engine's transaction state, which is per-process. If the same cart is completed concurrently from two servers, both requests may pass the "cart not yet completed" check and each create an order linked to the same cart. I expect one_order_per_cart (and possibly no_missing_orders) to fail when both requests return orders for one cart.

reserveInventoryStep reserves at item.location_ids[0], while the availability check in prepare-confirm-inventory-input picks locations with sufficient availability (filtering location_ids). If the first listed location lacks stock but another has it, the reservation may be written to a location whose level does not cover the units, producing reservations exceeding that level's stock. With the seeded single-location catalog this may not trigger, so I expect a pass, with no_oversell the check most likely to fail if it does.

The inventory module updates reserved_quantity by reading the level (level.reserved_quantity) and writing MathBN.add(level.reserved_quantity, adjustment) without a row lock or atomic increment. If two reservation creations on the same level interleave, one adjustment is lost, so the reserved counter falls behind the sum of live reservations. I expect reserved_matches_reservations to fail when several carts reserve the same WIDGET level concurrently across two servers. no_oversell may also fail if the lost update lets extra reservations through.

completeCartWorkflow checks whether the cart is already completed by reading cart state before creating the order. Two concurrent completions of the same cart on one server may both read "not completed" before either writes completed_at, so both create an order linked to that cart. I expect one_order_per_cart to fail (one cart linked to two orders, or two ok calls returning different order ids) in some runs.

The complete workflow creates the order and then links it to the cart and payment collection in separate steps. If a failure or race occurs between those steps, an order can be saved without its cart link, so a successful complete call returns an order id that is not linked to the cart. I expect no_missing_orders to fail for an ok completion whose order lacks a cart_orders row. This is a hypothesis from code structure, not observed behavior.

Same read-then-write path as before, but on the SOLO level with two servers releasing together, which maximizes overlap on one level's reserved_quantity update. I expect reserved_quantity to diverge from the live reservation sum if an adjustment is lost, which reserved_matches_reservations would report.

Stock checks may be done per cart line against available stock without adding up lines that share an inventory item. A cart with two lines for the same WIDGET (OVS-PIECE qty 6 plus OVS-TWOPACK qty 3 = 12 units) could each pass against 10 stocked. I expect no_oversell to fail if the cart completes with more than 10 units of WIDGET reserved.

Two carts share the WIDGET item, each with two lines that together need 6 units (OVS-PIECE x3 plus OVS-TWOPACK x... ), completed together from two servers. If each line is checked alone and lines are not summed per item, both carts can reserve against the 10 stocked units and exceed them. I expect no_oversell to fail when combined reservations exceed 10 WIDGET units.

Sequential completions of two WIDGET-sharing carts on different servers. If availability is read at one location while reservation writes at location_ids[0], a reservation could land on a level with insufficient stock. I expect no_oversell to fail if reservations exceed the level's stocked quantity. This is weak against a single-location catalog.

Several single-piece WIDGET carts completed concurrently from two servers, maximizing overlapping read-then-write updates to one WIDGET level's reserved_quantity. A lost adjustment would leave reserved_quantity below the live reservation sum, which reserved_matches_reservations reports.
